title: Browser sign-in: OIDC + PKCE
subtitle: Spring Security oauth2Login with the public client turfclub-web
summary: Every module UI signs people in with the OpenID Connect Authorization Code flow and PKCE (S256), using the public client turfclub-web. Spring Security applies PKCE automatically because the registration's client authentication method is none; the ID token's roles claim becomes ROLE_* authorities.

sections.title: The flow
sections.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant B as Browser
  participant S as Module (e.g. :8103)
  participant K as Keycloak
  B->>S: GET /horses (no session)
  S->>B: 302 /oauth2/authorization/keycloak
  B->>S: GET /oauth2/authorization/keycloak
  S->>B: 302 authorize?client_id=turfclub-web&code_challenge=…&method=S256&state&nonce
  B->>K: sign-in page (or SSO cookie)
  K->>B: 302 /login/oauth2/code/keycloak?code&state
  B->>S: callback
  S->>K: POST token (code + code_verifier, no secret)
  K->>S: id_token, access_token
  S->>S: verify id_token (JWKS, iss, aud, nonce), map roles → ROLE_*
  S->>B: 302 /horses (session cookie)

sections.title: application.yml (every service)
sections.code:
security:
  oauth2:
    client:
      registration:
        keycloak:
          client-id: turfclub-web
          client-authentication-method: none          # public client -> Spring applies PKCE (S256)
          authorization-grant-type: authorization_code
          redirect-uri: "{baseUrl}/login/oauth2/code/{registrationId}"
          scope: openid,profile,email
      provider:
        keycloak:
          issuer-uri: ${KEYCLOAK_ISSUER:http://localhost:8080/realms/turfclub}
          user-name-attribute: preferred_username
    resourceserver:
      jwt:
        issuer-uri: ${KEYCLOAK_ISSUER:http://localhost:8080/realms/turfclub}
        audiences: turfclub-api

sections.title: Web filter chain
Mapping the roles claim
Things to point out on camera
items: No client secret anywhere in the browser flow: PKCE replaces it for a public client.
The saved request sends the user back to the page they asked for; setMatchingRequestParameterName(null) removes Spring's ?continue marker.
ProvisioningLoginSuccessHandler records the sign-in in identity_security.app_user and a security event, which is why users appear in Core's Security screen only after their first sign-in.
Single sign-on: the second module redirects to Keycloak, finds the SSO cookie and returns immediately without a password prompt.
